neighbours.label: the negative or un- word right after a negator, i.e. understatement by cancelling a bad word (not bad, isn't half bad, not uncommon, not unlike, hardly unusual, not unpleasant, not difficult, not without); quiet on the same word with no negator (it was bad, an uncommon sight) and on negated ordinary or positive words (not hot, not good, not safe, not common); weaker after 'nothing'
neighbours.short: bad/un- word cancelled by a negator (not bad, not uncommon)
fire: The new pizza place downtown is not bad at all.
Honestly, for a first attempt, that painting isn't half bad.
It is not uncommon for hikers to get lost on that trail in winter.
Her voice sounded not unlike a church bell ringing across the valley.
Finding a parking spot on a Sunday is hardly unusual around here.
The cold swim in the lake was not unpleasant once we got used to it.
Assembling the bookshelf was not difficult, even without the instructions.
His plan, while clever, was not without its risks.
quiet: The new pizza place downtown is bad, sadly.
Honestly, for a first attempt, that painting is half finished.
It is uncommon for hikers to get lost on that trail in summer.
Her voice sounded unlike anything we had heard across the valley.
Finding a parking spot on a Sunday is unusual around here.
The cold swim in the lake was unpleasant from start to finish.
Assembling the bookshelf was difficult, even with the instructions.
His plan, while clever, was not safe for anyone involved.
